title: Personal Credit Cards: Size of a Points Deposit Restoring an Autopay Account
content:
This page fixes how many Personal Credit Cards points are redeemed into an overdrawn autopay checking account, and the cash that deposit delivers.

## Rule

- Where there is no shortfall, nothing is redeemed.
- Where the card's unredeemed points fall below the tier's smallest redemption, nothing is redeemed either.
- Otherwise the points redeemed are the larger of the points needed to cover the shortfall and the tier's smallest redemption. If the card's unredeemed points are fewer than that larger figure, every unredeemed point is redeemed instead.
- The cash delivered is the number of points redeemed multiplied by the tier's cash worth per point, rounded half-up to the cent.

## Decision table (hypothetical figures; the smallest redemption is set at an illustrative 3000 points, not any tier's figure)

| Shortfall | Points needed | Unredeemed points | Points redeemed |
|---|---|---|---|
| present | 1240 | 9000 | 3000, the smallest redemption being the larger figure |
| present | 5735 | 9000 | 5735 |
| present | 5735 | 4100 | 4100, all that the card holds |
| present | 5735 | 2200 | none, the card holds less than the smallest redemption |
| none | none | 9000 | none |

## Points of judgement

- A deposit may overshoot the shortfall when the smallest redemption is larger than the points needed; the larger figure still governs.
- A deposit may fall short of the shortfall when the card holds too few points; the card's whole unredeemed balance then goes, provided it reaches the smallest redemption.
